title: Signature Dependency Trust Ledger
description: Signature edition: every dependency carries a trust record — vetting date, reviewer, provenance level, and the policy version that approved it. The ledger answers 'why do we trust this package?' for every entry in the lockfile, and trust expires on schedule, forcing re-vetting. This is a Signature original method.
method: Record (package, vetting, reviewer, provenance) per dependency; expire trust on schedule; re-vet before renewal.
usage: Vet before first use; renew on schedule; revoke trust on any incident.

demo.code:
print('lodash@4.17.21: vetted 2026-01-15 by renee, SLSA L3, trust expires 2027-01-15')
print('expiry approaching -> re-vet queued')

title: Signature Dependency-confusion defenses
description: Signature edition: Dependency confusion attacks publish malicious public packages with the same names as private ones; resolvers that prefer public registries install the attacker's code. Defenses: scoped registries, explicit registry-per-dependency mapping, and verification that private names never resolve publicly.
method: Pin each dependency to its registry; block public resolution of private namespaces; verify hashes against the private registry.
usage: Map every dependency to an explicit registry; alert on any public hit for a private name.

demo.code:
print('dep @acme/auth: pinned to registry.acme.internal')
print('public registry hit for @acme/auth -> BLOCKED (confusion attempt?)')

title: Signature Typosquat detection
description: Signature edition: Attackers publish 'lodahs' next to 'lodash'; typosquat detectors compare new package names against popular ones (edit distance, confusables) and flag or block near-misses. Combined with popularity thresholds (new packages with famous-like names need review), it catches the oldest supply-chain trick.
method: Compute name similarity to popular packages; flag confusables; require review for suspicious new names.
usage: Run on every new package entering the mirror; block automatic mirroring of flagged names.

demo.code:
print('new package "lodahs": edit distance 1 from "lodash" (10M downloads)')
print('FLAGGED: typosquat suspected -> manual review required')

title: Signature Namespace-scoped registries
description: Signature edition: Registries support scopes (@acme/*) mapped to specific registry URLs; the resolver never consults the public registry for scoped names. Scoping is the simple, effective confusion defense — private names live in a namespace the public internet can't claim.
method: Configure scope -> registry mappings; enforce at the resolver; audit that no private name resolves publicly.
usage: Scope all private packages; enforce mappings in CI; audit for scope leaks.

demo.code:
print('scopes: @acme/* -> registry.acme.internal')
print('@acme/auth resolves ONLY via internal registry')

title: Signature Dependency firewall rules
description: Signature edition: Like a network firewall for packages: rules specifying which registries, versions, licenses, and publishers are allowed, enforced at resolve time. 'Only these publishers, only these licenses, nothing unpublished in the last 24h' — policy as code for the supply chain.
method: Write allow/deny rules; enforce in the resolver/proxy; log decisions; review rule hits.
usage: Start permissive with logging, tighten based on hits; review the rules quarterly.

demo.code:
rules = ['allow: registry.internal', 'deny: license=GPL', 'deny: age<24h']
print('rules:', rules)
print('request lodash (MIT, 5y old, internal): ALLOW')

title: Signature Offline build verification
description: Signature edition: Verify the build works with zero network: run the full build in a network-namespaced sandbox and confirm success. If the build secretly phones home (for a dependency, a license check, telemetry), the sandbox exposes it — offline verification proves the dependency closure is complete and honest.
method: Build in a no-network namespace; require success; log any blocked connection attempts as findings.
usage: Run offline builds in CI; investigate every blocked connection.

demo.code:
print('build in netns (no network): SUCCESS')
print('blocked attempts: 0 -> dependency closure complete and honest')

title: Signature Air-gapped dependency vendoring
description: Signature edition: The strongest isolation: vendor all dependencies into the repo (or a versioned bundle) on a connected machine, then build air-gapped from the vendor directory. No network resolution at build time means no exfiltration, no confusion, no MITM — the build's inputs are exactly the vendored bytes.
method: Vendor on a trusted machine; verify hashes; build offline from vendor/; the build never touches the network.
usage: Use for the most sensitive builds; re-vendor deliberately, not continuously.

demo.code:
print('vendor/: 142 packages, hashes verified')
print('build --offline: 0 network calls -> SUCCESS (air-gapped)')

title: Signature Mirrored registries with verification
description: Signature edition: Organizations mirror public registries internally and vet what enters: new packages are scanned, reviewed, and only then mirrored. Developers resolve against the mirror, never the wild internet — the mirror is the trust boundary, and everything inside it is allowlisted.
method: Proxy all fetches through the mirror; vet new packages before mirroring; sign mirrored artifacts; developers use the mirror exclusively.
usage: Make the mirror the only allowed source; automate vetting; sign everything mirrored.

demo.code:
print('request: lodash@4.17.21 -> mirror: vetted, signed, served')
print('new package leftpad-x: QUARANTINED pending review')

title: Signature Lockfile hash verification
description: Signature edition: The lockfile pins exact versions and content hashes; the resolver verifies every downloaded artifact against the lockfile before use. Even a compromised mirror can't substitute code — the hash won't match. The lockfile is the trust anchor; the registry is just a dumb byte store.
method: Verify SHA-512 (or better) per artifact at install; fail closed on mismatch; commit lockfiles; review lockfile diffs.
usage: Verify hashes in CI and on developer machines; treat hash mismatches as security incidents.

demo.code:
import hashlib
expected = hashlib.sha256(b'pkg-bytes').hexdigest()
print('download hash:', expected[:12], '== lockfile:', expected[:12], '-> INSTALL')
